title: Introduce microeconomy-autopilot: tenant-aware defaults, quant profile discovery
author: Priya Nambiar
description:
Motivation: customers frequently accept conservative batching/cache defaults and a single quant profile; this inflates unit cost and increases coldstart latency. This PR introduces the "microeconomy-autopilot" subsystem: a lightweight control-plane component that (1) samples tenant workload shapes, (2) proposes batching and cache defaults scoped to tenant/route, (3) performs non-disruptive quant-profile discovery using cached small evals, and (4) exposes a dry-run CLI and telemetry tags for safe rollouts.

What this PR does (summary):
- Add a new package pkg/econ/autopilot which implements the sampling+scoring pipeline and a rules engine to suggest defaults.
- Introduce an autosuggester CLI (cmd/rwctl autosuggest) to preview recommended batch/cache/quant presets per-tenant.
- Wire minimal nonblocking integration into the serving runtime so suggestions are only applied when tenant opt-in is set; includes safe fallbacks and canary rollout helpers.
- Create telemetry tags and tracing spans for decision provenance and action-attribution.
- Add python SDK helper to fetch and display suggested defaults (sdk/python/redwood/econ_suggester.py).

Design notes: the autopilot is conservative by default: suggestions are scored with an uncertainty band; suggestions include a rollback TTL and compatibility checks (e.g., quant profile must pass small end-to-end output-similarity checks before being recommended). The sampling engine uses low-overhead request mirrors and a probabilistic sampler to avoid production load.

Checklist:
- [x] core sampling pipeline and rule scorer implemented
- [x] dry-run CLI and SDK helper added
- [x] minimal serving integration with tenant opt-in flags
- [x] unit and integration tests (including a small simulated tenant workload)
- [x] telemetry and spans for auditability

Testing and verification: ran unit tests and a simulated tenant run in preprod. Addressed a flaky fixture in batching_test by switching to time-agnostic assertions. e2e smoke in staging with a canary tenant shows ~18% token-cost reduction for a synthetic conversational workload without regressions in top-1 completion diffs (measured by our eval harness).

Rollout plan: ship as feature-flagged behind autosuggest.enabled=false by default. We'll enable autosuggest for internal tenants only for 2 weeks, evaluate telemetry, then propose opt-in for a subset of customers. Safeguards: suggestion TTL, automatic rollback on quality regression, and a dry-run mode for SRE/SEs.

Related: ENG-1429 implements the decision scoring primitives used by this PR; SUP-5789 requested tenant-level default suggestions after customer incident.

review_comments: Ethan Cole: Overall great work. A few concerns: the quant discovery path appears to run small evals inline — can we ensure this never touches production model weights or unredacted inputs? Please add encryption/KMS checks.

Priya Nambiar (author): Good point. The discovery harness runs on a read-only inference variant and strips PII; I added a note and explicit KMS integration check in autopilot.go and the config. See commit 'security: enforce kms checks for discovery'.
Marta Ruiz: The scoring fn needs clearer weighting between unit-cost delta and expected quality delta. Can we expose tunable weights per-tenant?
Priya Nambiar: Added tenant-scoped overrides in configs/autopilot_defaults.yaml and a runtime CLI to modify weights. Also added a test that checks weight override precedence.
Liam O'Connor: CI showed a flaky e2e earlier — looks fixed. Approving pending a changelog entry.
Priya Nambiar: Added docs/rwctl-autosuggest.md and a short release note in configs/autopilot_defaults.yaml.
